title: Component descriptor definitions
description: Shared component definitions (F2-02, schema-strategy). NON-NORMATIVE machine artifact: the normative source is spec/package/component-types.md and spec/package/layout.md. A component is a typed, addressable element; a file is not a component merely because it exists.

componentDescriptor.description: Base component descriptor. A component MUST declare its type; a component whose type cannot be determined MUST cause rejection. F1: package/component-types.md §2; package/layout.md §3.7.

type.description: The recognized component type. Exactly eight are recognized at v1alpha1, and the list is exhaustive: a new type MUST be admitted through the extension process. There is NO 'Tool' component type: entries under tools/ are composed through the adopted tool-interop standard and are not a competing component type. F1: package/component-types.md §2; package/layout.md §4.1.

name.description: Component name (slug grammar). F1: package/layout.md §2; core/identity.md §2.

path.description: Package-relative path of the component content. Component paths MUST be relative to the package root and MUST NOT contain '..' or otherwise escape it. F1: package/layout.md §2.1.

payload.description: Type-specific descriptor payload for the component. The Policy language and the workflow graph are OPEN (decision record §58, open question 'policy language / workflow graph'): a component is a descriptor, not a DSL, so this position is permissive and MUST NOT fix a policy language, execute code or define a workflow schema. F1: package/component-types.md §6.4, §9.3.
